resources.string: Use this tablet as a second display for your Mac.
Connect the tablet to your Mac with a USB cable, or over Wi-Fi.
Start the Ligarview host on your Mac. This tablet connects on its own.
The Mac is ready over USB. Tap Connect to start the display.
Android is asking whether Ligarview may use the USB accessory. Tap OK on the dialog.
Start the Ligarview host on your Mac. This tablet connects as soon as it is ready.
Trying again. Make sure the Ligarview host is running on your Mac. (%1$s)
Start the Ligarview host on your Mac
It creates the extra display and waits for the tablet.
Plug the tablet into the Mac
Use a cable that carries data, not a charge-only one.
Tap OK when Android asks to open Ligarview
Tick “Use by default” and it will not ask again.
No USB debugging or developer mode needed.
Both devices must be on the same network. 5 GHz Wi-Fi works best. You can find the Mac’s address in System Settings › Network.
All set. Your tablet is ready.
The display runs at %1$d Hz, so the cursor and window dragging feel smooth.
Turn on the high refresh rate
The display runs at %1$d Hz but supports up to %2$d Hz. In Settings › Display › Motion smoothness, choose Adaptive (or High).
Nothing is limiting the display or the processor.
Power saving lowers the refresh rate and slows the video decoder. Switch it off while you use the tablet as a monitor.
Allowed to run in the background
Android will not close Ligarview to save battery.
Android can close idle apps overnight. Exclude Ligarview from battery optimization (on Samsung: Battery › Background usage limits › Never auto sleeping apps).
USB 2 is enough. A USB 3 cable and port give extra headroom. The tablet charges over the same cable.
While streaming, long-press the picture for statistics. Back returns to this screen.
